name: A Muddy Bizarre Adventure
description: The Sumeru researcher Khedive, who is conducting research as part of the exploration team, seems to be troubled about the environment within The Chasm.

dialogs.content: Didn't you say that theoretically, there wouldn't be any problems?
The Spike wound up causing the dark mud to gush out instead...
Ah, is that how it is... Agh, to think that I did not factor the ground into my calculations. Ah, what an error.
Factor the ground into your calculations?
That's right. Our previous experiments all took place on softer soil.

But within The Chasm, the medium through which the Spike's energy travels is not soil but rock, which has very different properties. This caused a major discrepancy between the earlier calculations and the actual results.
Indeed, theory is not a mere matter of imagination. Instead, it must be grounded and proven in reality.
This proving process seems kinda dangerous, though. Also, why did so much mud come out all at once?
Indeed, this place is quite far from the mining complex, so the mud really shouldn't be flowing all the way here... The situation must be more urgent than we imagined.
Also, the Pursina's Spike has a definite effect on environments affected by the dark mud. This shows that the mud's proliferation is, as I guessed, an issue that stems from the Ley Lines.
This proves the need for experimentation and proof, does it not?
Of course, if I had done the experiment myself, I would have wound up being attacked by the monsters.

Not that I worry about being injured — that would be a small loss compared to any damage that might be done to the Pursina's Spike. How would I answer to our great tutor Firnas or my fellow researchers in the Kshahrewar...
You should pay more attention to your own safety nonetheless.

True. The data we've collected can be used to adjust the results of our calculations. Now, the solutions to these interfering parameters... I believe there are four such methods, though there should be only one that will prove most effective.
#Thank you so much for helping me with this test run, {NICKNAME}. I will make some adjustments to the Pursina's Spike.
Later, it can be moved into the mining complex, where operations can then begin.
You're moving it into the mining complex?
Well, no. I had agreed with Khedive to hire some of the local miners here to move it.
But when they heard that my objective was to resolve the issue of the dark mud, they refused any payment.
I've spoken to Khedive and Muning from the Ministry of Civil Affairs, however. The Mora will still go to them as compensation.
Of course, I'll need you to help start the machine up once it reaches its destination.
By yourself?
